title: Vice-President Inaugurates Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026 in Kozhikode
subtitle:
“Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi: India’s progress and cultural heritage are complementary to each other”: Vice-President

“Diverse Traditions, One Dharma: India’s Shared Civilisational Heritage Is Its Enduring Strength”: Vice-President

Navaratri reminds us that courage must overcome fear, righteousness must prevail over injustice, and knowledge must dispel ignorance: Vice-President

Vice-President Releases “Sangha Noottandile Akshara Mudrakal” at Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 6:57PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026 in Kozhikode, Keralam, and emphasised the importance of preserving India’s rich cultural heritage while advancing on the path of development.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the Navaratri Sargotsavam 2026 in Kozhikode, Keralam today. 

Vice President expressed hope that Navaratri Sargotsavam would inspire the youth, encourage artists and strengthen efforts to preserve India’s cultural heritage while embracing innovation. 

He congratulated Kesari Weekly on organising the festival and commended its contribution to Malayalam journalism, democratic values and freedom of expression.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 16, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that Navaratri celebrates the divine feminine power of Adi Parashakti, the eternal source of creation, strength, wisdom and compassion. He observed that the festival’s enduring message is that courage must overcome fear, righteousness must prevail over injustice, and knowledge must dispel ignorance. These timeless values, he said, continue to guide society towards a better future.
Highlighting India’s diverse Navaratri traditions, the Vice-President said that despite the diversity of languages, traditions and forms of worship, the country remains united by its shared civilisational heritage. This, he noted, reflects the spirit of “Ek Bharat, Shreshtha Bharat”.
Emphasising the Prime Minister’s vision of “Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi”, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that India’s cultural heritage and developmental aspirations complement each other. Drawing an analogy with the banyan tree, he observed that just as a tree draws strength from its deep roots while spreading its branches, India’s traditions and values provide stability, identity and continuity as the nation embraces modernity and progress.
The Vice-President congratulated Kesari Weekly on organising the festival and commended its contribution to Malayalam journalism, democratic values and freedom of expression.
On the occasion, the Vice-President released the book “Sangha Noottandile Akshara Mudrakal”. He also presented the Sarga Kesari Award to Shri P. R. Rajendran in recognition of his contribution to the fine arts.
Shri Radhakrishnan expressed hope that Navaratri Sargotsavam would inspire the youth, encourage artists and strengthen efforts to preserve India’s cultural heritage while embracing innovation. Praying for the blessings of the Goddesses, he expressed hope that society would find the strength to fight injustice, share prosperity with the underprivileged, and apply knowledge towards building a compassionate society that cares for all.
Shri Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar, Hon’ble Governor of Keralam and Tamil Nadu; Shri C. Sadanandan Master, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha; Smt. Vidhu-bala, President, Navaratri Sargotsavam Samiti; Shri A. K. Prasanth, Working President, Navaratri Sargotsavam Samiti; and other dignitaries were present on the occasion.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan Commissions Indian Navy’s First Indigenous Multi-Purpose Vessel INS Samarthak at Karwar
subtitle:
INS Samarthak, with over 75 per cent indigenous content, reflects India’s growing self-reliance in defence manufacturing: Vice-President

“Indian Navy Stands Ever-Vigilant and Combat-Ready to Safeguard India’s Maritime Interests”: Vice-President

“INS Samarthak Reflects the Growing Role of India’s Private Shipbuilding Industry”: Vice-President

“Karwar Symbolises Both India’s Glorious Maritime Heritage and Its Maritime Future”: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 3:08PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today commissioned INS Samarthak, the Indian Navy’s first indigenous Multi-Purpose Vessel, at Karwar, Karnataka. The commissioning marks a significant milestone in India’s journey towards self-reliance in defence manufacturing and the development of advanced indigenous naval capabilities.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan today commissioned INS Samarthak, the Indian Navy’s first indigenous Multi-Purpose Vessel, at Karwar, Karnataka.

With over 75% indigenous content, INS Samarthak reflects India’s growing self-reliance in defence manufacturing and will support trials of next-generation weapons, sensors and unmanned systems.

A significant milestone towards a stronger, technologically advanced and Aatmanirbhar Indian Navy.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
October 16, 2026
Addressing the gathering, the Vice-President said that INS Samarthak, with more than 75 per cent indigenous content, reflects the growing strength of India’s industrial, technological and shipbuilding capabilities. He observed that self-reliance in defence is no longer merely an aspiration but an emerging reality, contributing to India’s strategic autonomy and the vision of a Viksit and Aatmanirbhar Bharat articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi.
Highlighting India’s rich maritime heritage, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan recalled the naval traditions of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj and the Chola dynasty, which extended India’s maritime influence across the Indian Ocean and Southeast Asia.
The Vice-President commended the Indian Navy for its distinguished service in safeguarding national sovereignty and maritime interests. He also appreciated its role as a first responder and a preferred security partner in the Indian Ocean Region, including anti-piracy operations, the evacuation of Indian citizens and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief missions.
Highlighting the significance of INS Samarthak, the Vice-President said that the vessel will serve as a versatile platform for trials and evaluation of next-generation weapons, sensors and emerging technologies. Its capabilities will also support maritime surveillance and reconnaissance, offshore patrolling, launch and recovery of targets, operations involving unmanned systems, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. He observed that such a platform would enable the Navy to adapt more rapidly to emerging technological developments and translate indigenous innovation into operational capabilities.
Referring to Karwar’s strategic importance, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that its deep natural harbour and proximity to the Arabian Sea make it a vital component of India’s maritime security architecture. He highlighted the ongoing development of modern naval infrastructure under Project Seabird, which is enhancing the Navy’s capacity to base and sustain ships and submarines while generating wider economic opportunities for the region.
The Vice-President also underscored the growing partnership between the Indian Navy, defence public sector undertakings, private shipyards, DRDO, academia, MSMEs and start-ups in strengthening India’s defence manufacturing ecosystem. Appreciating Larsen & Toubro (L&T) for its contribution to the project, he acknowledged the efforts of naval designers, production authorities, shipyard professionals, engineers, technicians, suppliers and ancillary industries in building indigenous naval capabilities.
Admiral Krishna Swaminathan, Chief of the Naval Staff; Vice-Admiral Sanjay Vatsayan, Flag Officer Commanding-in-Chief; Vice-Admiral Sanjay Sadhu, Controller Warship Production and Acquisition; Rear Admiral Vikram Menon, Flag Officer (Karnataka); retired Rear Admiral G. title: ITRA Jamnagar Hosts National Conference “Ayu-Tech Navonmesh 2026” on the Integration of Ayurveda and Artificial Intelligence
subtitle: National and International Experts Deliberate on Responsible AI and Digital Innovation in Ayurveda at ITRA Jamnagar
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 9:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A national conference on “AI and Ayurveda” was held under “Ayu-Tech Navonmesh 2026” on the occasion of the 6th Foundation Day of the Institute of Teaching and Research in Ayurveda (ITRA), Jamnagar. The conference held extensive deliberations on integrating Ayurveda with modern digital technology, the role of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in research, and the possibilities for its responsible use in healthcare services.
In a conversation with ITRA’s channel Ayush Next Communication Network (ANCN) on the sidelines of the event, Dr. Geetha Krishnan, Head of the Traditional Medicine Research, Data and Innovation Unit, WHO-GTMC, said: “Artificial Intelligence (AI) holds immense potential to understand Ayurveda better and make its application more effective. However, before adopting any new technology, a deep understanding of the fundamental principles of Ayurveda science is essential. AI should work as a complement to Ayurveda, not replace its core knowledge and wisdom. Maintaining the authenticity of Ayurveda while exploring the possibilities of modern technologies is an important responsibility of the Ayurveda world. By adopting a balanced approach, we can harness the potential of AI without compromising the core principles of Ayurveda. Establishing the right balance between tradition and innovation is our collective responsibility. Only by doing so can we take Ayurveda forward in a meaningful, effective and sustainable manner.”
Prof. Dr. Tanuja Nesari, Director, ITRA Jamnagar, said that Ayu-Tech Navonmesh 2026 has proved to be an important platform for innovation and collaboration for the future of Ayurveda. She said it provided an important platform to encourage dialogue between traditional Ayurvedic knowledge and advanced technology, and furthered discussion on the ethical, scientific and practical aspects of the potential use of AI in Ayurvedic research, education, drug development and healthcare services.
Shri Sameer Pujari, AI Lead, Digital Health and Innovation (DHI), WHO Headquarters, highlighted the potential of AI in the preservation of knowledge. He emphasised the global collaboration among WHO, the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), ongoing since 2018, to advance AI applications in health. He also discussed the risks and challenges associated with AI, including ethical aspects, data privacy and regulatory barriers, particularly in the context of traditional medicine.
Shri Naman Goyal, Officer on Special Duty (OSD), Ayush Grid, Ministry of Ayush, said that the basic concepts, applications and working of AI and Machine Learning (ML) were covered, including key processes such as data collection, data processing, model training, testing and prediction. AI-driven chatbots and key digital tools under Ayush Grid were also showcased, and the presentation underlined the important role of these tools in strengthening digital health services and advancing technology-based Ayush services.
The conference aimed to link Ayurveda’s rich traditional knowledge with modern digital technology and encourage new possibilities in research, innovation and healthcare services. Ayurveda scholars, researchers, academicians, technology experts and national and international delegates shared their views, in person and online, across the sessions on the effective, ethical and scientific use of AI. Discussions covered potential applications of AI in Ayurvedic drug research and development, quality assurance, clinical trials and education, with special emphasis on integrating traditional knowledge with modern data-based methods, making research more effective, encouraging new product development and advancing technology-based healthcare services.
Thematic Sessions and Expert Participation
Sessions and expert discussions were held on the following themes:
Artificial Intelligence, digital knowledge and global transformation in traditional medicine systems
Responsible AI for Ayurveda: ethics, scientific evidence and innovation
The potential of AI-based Ayurveda, from traditional practices to intelligent healthcare services
Use of AI for innovation, product development and responsible clinical trials in Ayurveda
Experts from various reputed national and international institutions participated as keynote and principal speakers. They included Prof. Shubhada Nagarkar (Professor and Head, Department of Library and Information Science, and Coordinator, Centre for Publication Ethics (CPE), Savitribai Phule Pune University); Dr. Rajiv Vasudevan (Founder, Managing Director and CEO, Apollo Ayurveda Hospitals, Bengaluru); and Dr. Sumer Singh (Associate Professor, Department of Design, IIT Delhi).
Other speakers from the fields of Ayurveda and AI included Dr. Maki Kajiwara (Technical Officer, WHO-GTMC); Dr. Girish Tillu (Principal Investigator–Ayush, Centre of Excellence, Department of Health Sciences, Savitribai Phule Pune University); Dr. Sandeep Kale (Assistant Professor, Department of Rasashastra and Vikriti Vigyan, R. A. Podar Government Ayurved Medical College, Mumbai); Dr. Rajeshwari Singh (Senior Adviser, Data, Digital Health, Analytics and AI, Health Systems Division, WHO, Switzerland); Prof. (Dr.) Mitali Mukherjee (Professor, Department of Biosciences and Bioengineering, IIT Jodhpur); Dr. Santosh Dixit (Principal Domain Expert, Healthcare and Life Sciences, Persistent Systems); Dr. Ganesh Karaikhede (Healthcare Domain Expert, AI QT Group, C-DAC, Pune); and Dr. Bala Pesala (Founder and CEO,
Ayur.AI
).
The 6th Foundation Day of ITRA Jamnagar was celebrated yesterday, 15 October 2026, as “ITRA Day”, with strategic MoUs and collaborative initiatives, expert lectures, discussions on AI and Ayurveda, and institutional honours and awards. ITRA is the country’s first Ayurveda institute to be granted the status of Institute of National Importance, dedicated to the nation by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 15 October 2020. Over the past six years, its NABH-accredited 300-bed hospital has provided consultation and treatment to 18,47,807 patients through 22 OPDs and treated 27,520 patients in the IPD. The Institute also marked one year of its official TV channel, ANCN, and offers courses in Ayurveda, Ayurveda pharmacy, Yoga and Naturopathy.
The conference reaffirmed the commitment of ITRA to advancing Ayurveda through responsible AI, with tradition and innovation moving forward together.

title: AIIA Marks a Decade of Service with Over 37.74 Lakh Patients Treated Across Its Healthcare Network
subtitle: Decade-Long Journey Highlights Expanding Clinical Services, Research and Quality Education in Ayurveda
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 7:36PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The All India Institute of Ayurveda (AIIA), New Delhi, has released a report highlighting its achievements over the past decade, documenting the expansion of its clinical services and healthcare outreach. According to the report, a total of 37,74,524 patients received healthcare services across the institute’s main campus and affiliated and outreach centres between October 2016 and September 2026. The milestone reflects the institute’s growing clinical reach and its continued efforts to strengthen Ayurveda-based healthcare through quality patient care, education and research.
Of the total patients served, approximately 30,37,077 received healthcare services at AIIA’s main campus in Sarita Vihar, New Delhi. The institute’s clinical infrastructure includes outpatient department (OPD) services with the capacity to attend to approximately 3,000 patients daily and a 200-bed inpatient department (IPD), enabling it to cater to a large and diverse patient population.
Beyond its main campus, AIIA has expanded its healthcare outreach through its satellite centre in Goa and affiliated and outreach facilities at Safdarjung Hospital, the UPSC Building, the National Cancer Institute at Jhajjar, the IAS Training Centre in Mussoorie, and Kevadia, Ekta Nagar. These centres collectively served approximately 7.37 lakh patients during the reporting period, extending the reach of the institute’s clinical services to more people.
According to AIIA Director Prof. (Vaidya) P. K. Prajapati, public interest in Ayurveda increased significantly during the COVID-19 pandemic and in the subsequent years. He noted that patient footfall at the institute had increased more than fourfold, reflecting the growing demand for Ayurveda-based consultations and treatment. The institute attended to approximately 1.23 lakh patients in 2020, with the number rising to over 5.40 lakh by September 2026.
The release of the decade-long report on Foundation Day, alongside the organisation of KAUMARACON-2026, underscores AIIA’s focus on expanding access to clinical services while strengthening the role of Ayurveda through scientific research, quality education and institutional collaboration. The institute continues to work towards integrating traditional medical knowledge with contemporary healthcare approaches and advancing evidence-informed practices in Ayurveda.
The All India Institute of Ayurveda, New Delhi, is an autonomous institution under the Ministry of Ayush, Government of India. It is dedicated to advancing healthcare, education, research and innovation in Ayurveda, while promoting the national and international recognition of India’s traditional systems of medicine.

title: Ayush Innovation Sees Eightfold Rise in Patent Filings
subtitle:
Report on Ayush inventions highlights rapid growth in innovation and Intellectual Property activity

Maharashtra Leads Ayush Patent Activity with 744 Filings and 142 Grants
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 2:33PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Ayush-related innovation and intellectual property activity in India has witnessed a significant expansion over the past decade, with 4,077 patent applications filed and 711 patents granted between FY 2014–15 and FY 2025–26, according to the Status Report on Ayush Related Inventions in India (2014–2026) released during the celebrations of the 11th Ayurveda Day.
Published by the Office of the Controller General of Patents, Designs & Trademarks (CGPDTM), Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry, Government of India, the report provides an overview of the evolution of Ayush-related inventions and intellectual property activity in India over the period.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, reiterated, “The substantial growth in Ayush-related patent filings and grants reflects the increasing focus on research, innovation and intellectual property in the Ayush sector. The Government is committed to creating an enabling ecosystem where traditional knowledge, scientific research and contemporary innovation can contribute to new products, technologies and solutions while ensuring that India’s rich knowledge systems are appropriately protected.”
Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha, Secretary, Ministry of Ayush, emphasised, “The steady expansion of patent activity demonstrates the growing research and innovation base of the Ayush sector. The increasing participation of individuals, universities, research institutions, startups and industry is encouraging and will help strengthen the translation of research into innovative solutions. The Ministry will continue to support evidence generation, research collaboration and innovation across the Ayush ecosystem.”
The report highlights a sharp increase in patenting activity, with annual filings rising from 63 applications in FY 2014–15 to 590 applications in FY 2025–26, representing a growth of around 836.5 per cent. Patent filings peaked at 606 applications in FY 2022–23, then fell to 299 in FY 2023–24 before recovering to 590 by FY 2025–26. Annual patent grants also increased substantially, from 3 in FY 2015–16 to 204 in FY 2023–24.
The post-COVID period witnessed a particularly strong acceleration in patent activity. Between FY 2020–21 and FY 2025–26, 2,854 applications, or 70 per cent of total filings, were recorded, compared with 1,223 applications during FY 2014–15 to FY 2019–20. Similarly, 657 patents, accounting for 92.4 per cent of all grants, were awarded during the post-COVID period.
The expanding innovation ecosystem is reflected in the diversity of applicants. Natural persons accounted for 2,113 applications, or 51.9 per cent of total filings, and 398 grants, while educational institutions contributed 995 applications and 88 grants. Together, natural persons and educational institutions accounted for 76.3 per cent of total filings. Corporate and other entities accounted for 700 applications and 176 grants, while small entities and startups contributed 144 and 125 filings, respectively.
The findings of the report underline the growing integration of research, innovation, entrepreneurship and intellectual property protection within the Ayush ecosystem, with increasing participation from individual innovators, educational institutions, research organisations, startups and industry.

The campaign forms part of ECL's broader efforts to institutionalise cleanliness, streamline administrative processes and promote the efficient utilisation of resources across its establishments.

title: SECL Strengthens Digital Governance and Service Delivery under Special Campaign 6
subtitle: HMIS and PPO/Jeevan Pramaan Patra Portal to improve access to healthcare and pension-related services
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 3:28PM by PIB Delhi
content:
South Eastern Coalfields Limited (SECL), a subsidiary of Coal India Limited under the Ministry of Coal, is strengthening digital governance and citizen-centric service delivery through its Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) and PPO/Jeevan Pramaan Patra Portal. These initiatives align with the objectives of Special Campaign 6, promoting ease of access, administrative efficiency, transparency and paperless governance.
HMIS: Streamlining Healthcare Services
SECL's Hospital Management Information System (HMIS) provides an integrated digital platform for managing healthcare services. The system enables digital recording of patient registration, medical consultations, treatment and medication-related information, ensuring systematic maintenance of medical records and easier access to patients' medical histories.
HMIS also facilitates online processing of medical reimbursement claims, along with integration of AMRIT Pharmacy and medicine management, helping reduce paperwork, streamline administrative processes and improve healthcare service delivery.
PPO/Jeevan Pramaan Patra Portal: Ease of Access for Pensioners
SECL has developed a centralised PPO/Jeevan Pramaan Patra Portal to digitise the distribution of Pension Payment Orders (PPOs) and simplify annual Life Certificate submission for retired employees and surviving spouses.
The portal enables pensioners to access and download PPO documents online and submit annual Life Certificates digitally, reducing dependence on physical documentation and manual processes.
An integrated Governance Dashboard facilitates monitoring of PPO uploads and compliance across SECL's operational areas, improving transparency and administrative efficiency.
Promoting Good Governance through Digitalisation
The implementation phase of Special Campaign 6, being undertaken from 2 to 31 October 2026, focuses on cleanliness, e-waste management, space optimisation, record management and reduction of pendency.
SECL's digital initiatives complement these objectives by promoting paperless administration, improved accessibility, efficient record management and faster service delivery.
Through HMIS and the PPO/Jeevan Pramaan Patra Portal, SECL continues to advance digital transformation and good governance, making essential services more accessible and convenient for employees, pensioners and their families.

content:
In a significant step towards strengthening onion availability and ensuring affordable prices ahead of the festive season, the Department of Consumer Affairs is expanding the distribution of buffer onions under the Price Stabilization Fund (PSF), with the
first-ever Kanda Express movement to Agartala, Tripura.
The consignment, carrying approximately 440 MT of onions, is expected to reach Agartala by 18th October 2026.
The initiative marks a further expansion of the Government’s onion distribution network in the North-East, following the successful movement of buffer onions to Assam through Kanda Express. The dispatch to Agartala reinforces the Government’s commitment to expanding supply outreach, improving last-mile availability and ensuring timely access to affordable onions across consumption centres in all regions of the country.
Kanda Express to Strengthen Onion Distribution Across Tripura
The intervention is expected to enhance market coverage across seven of Tripura’s eight districts: Dhalai, South Tripura, Khowai, Unakoti, West Tripura, Gomati and Sepahijala.
So far, two Kanda Express rail rakes, carrying 840 MT and 452 MT of onions, respectively, and 44 truck consignments carrying a total of 1,513.46 MT
have supplied buffer onions across the North-East. The distribution has covered key locations in Assam, Tripura and Nagaland, including Kamrup, Guwahati, Gomati, Dimapur, Sepahijala, Kohima, Niuland and Chumoukedima.
The expansion of rail-based and road-based distribution is aimed at improving the reach of buffer stocks and supplementing market supplies in key consumption centres across the region.
Fresh Kharif Arrivals Improve Market Availability; Mandi Prices Moderate
With fresh Kharif arrivals gathering pace, onion mandi prices have moderated across major markets. The All-India average mandi price declined from a peak of approximately ₹3,600 per quintal in September to around ₹3,300 per quintal in October.
The calibrated releases from the onion buffer continue to supplement market supplies, improve availability and help moderate retail prices. The Department of Consumer Affairs is continuing these interventions in response to prevailing market conditions to support consumer access to onions at affordable prices.
Retail Onion Prices Decline in 211 Cities; Regional Price Differences Narrow
Over the past two weeks, 211 cities have reported a decline of ₹1–₹13 per kg in retail onion prices. The moderation has been observed across major consuming States and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Assam, Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Goa, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, Maharashtra, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Odisha, Punjab, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and West Bengal.
In Assam, retail onion prices have also moderated in recent weeks, with around 12 centres in the State recording a decline ranging from ₹1 to ₹8 per kg.
The disparity between Assam’s average retail onion prices and the All-India average has narrowed significantly over the past two years. Two years ago, the average retail price in Assam stood at ₹61.96 per kg, compared with the All-India average of ₹54.13 per kg, representing a difference of ₹7.83 per kg. Currently, Assam’s average retail price is ₹54.30 per kg, while the All-India average stands at ₹53.07 per kg, reducing the difference to ₹1.23 per kg.
This convergence indicates a substantial narrowing of the regional price differential, with retail onion prices in Assam now broadly aligned with the national average.
Onion Buffer Disposal to Continue Based on Market Conditions
The Government continues to closely monitor onion prices, market arrivals and supply conditions across the country. Disposal of onions from the Price Stabilization Fund (PSF) buffer stock is guided by prevailing market conditions, price trends and availability requirements.
Further releases will be undertaken, as required, in accordance with approved operational decisions to ensure adequate market availability and help moderate undue price volatility.

title: BHASHINI and IISc Bangaluru : Text-to-Speech Model for Sourashtra Language
subtitle: New AI-based Speech Technology Supports Digital Access, Preservation and Wider Use of a Low-Resource Indian Language
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 2:32PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening language technology for low-resource Indian languages, the Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), Bengaluru, has developed Text-to-Speech (TTS) models for Sourashtra, a minority Indo-Aryan language spoken predominantly by the Sourashtra community in Tamil Nadu.
The initiative aims to expand the availability of speech technology for languages that have limited digital resources and support their use in digital applications, language learning, accessibility solutions, documentation and research.
The newly developed models use the VITS (Variational Inference with adversarial learning for end-to-end Text-to-Speech) architecture and are capable of generating Sourashtra speech directly from text. The models include male and female voices, with each voice available for text written in both Tamil script and Sourashtra script. This enables users to work with Sourashtra in the scripts used for the language.
The models have been trained using a dedicated Sourashtra speech corpus developed at the SPIRE Lab, Indian Institute of Science, Bengaluru. The corpus contains more than 28 hours of gender-balanced speech recordings, including recordings from one male and one female voice artist. The corpus includes composed sentences as well as sentences drawn from literature, with transcriptions available in both Sourashtra and Tamil scripts.
AIKOSH: BHASHINI’s AIKOSH platform provides access to language datasets and resources that support the development of Indian language technologies. The SPICOR TTS 3.0 Sourashtra Corpus is now available on AIKOSH, offering 28+ hours of gender-balanced Sourashtra speech data developed at IISc Bengaluru. The corpus includes diverse and literary content in both Sourashtra and Tamil scripts, supporting the development of Sourashtra language technologies.
The male voice model was trained on approximately 10,000 utterances, while the female voice model was trained on approximately 11,400 utterances. The speech corpus and associated text data were carefully prepared and cleaned to support the development of the TTS models.
The models generate audio at 22,050 Hz and operate directly on character-level text, eliminating the need for a separate phonemizer. The four models comprise two speaker voices, each available in Tamil-script and Sourashtra-script versions.
Sourashtra, spoken by around 2.48 lakh people according to the 2011 Census, has a relatively limited digital presence and fewer available speech technology resources. The development of these models goes beyond language preservation by helping bring Sourashtra into the digital ecosystem. The technology can benefit the Sourashtra-speaking community by enabling access to digital content in their language, support students and language learners through speech-enabled learning tools, and improve accessibility for users who rely on spoken digital content. At the same time, the availability of the models and underlying speech resources provides researchers, developers and institutions with a foundation to build further Sourashtra language technologies and applications across education, accessibility and other public-facing digital services.
The models can support applications including reading Sourashtra text aloud, language learning, accessibility solutions and research in low-resource speech synthesis, while contributing to the broader development of digital resources for Sourashtra and other underrepresented Indian languages.
Through collaborations with academic and research institutions, BHASHINI continues to strengthen the ecosystem for Indian-language datasets, speech technologies and AI-based language solutions, particularly for languages that remain underrepresented in the digital domain.
About Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD)
The Digital India BHASHINI Division (DIBD), under the Digital India Corporation (DIC), Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), is building a national ecosystem for AI-powered multilingual digital inclusion. BHASHINI supports 36 Indian text languages, 23 Indian voice languages and 35 international languages, and enables the integration of Language AI capabilities across government and public-facing digital services. Its ecosystem includes technologies for translation, speech recognition, speech synthesis, transliteration and other language services, helping make digital information and services more accessible across India's linguistic diversity.

title: CAQM expands PTZ Camera-based Remote Monitoring to all Industries covered under Direction No. 98 in NCR
subtitle: PTZ Cameras to be installed by 30th November 2026

content:
The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) has strengthened the mechanism for remote monitoring of air-polluting industries in the National Capital Region (NCR)
by
exten
ding
the requirement for installation and operationalization of Pan-Tilt-Zoom (PTZ) cameras to all categories of industries covered under Statutory Direction No. 98
. T
h
is will
expand the scope of technology-enabled monitoring of fuel usage, industrial emissions and compliance with prescribed pollution-control measures. The Order supersedes the Commission’s earlier Order dated 05.10.2026.
The Commission has directed that all 17 categories of highly polluting industries identified by CPCB, Red Category (Medium and Large) air-polluting industries, Food & Food Processing and Textile industries having boilers/ thermic fluid heaters, and Metal industries having furnaces, operating in NCR, shall ensure compliance with the following requirements:
(i) Installation and positioning of PTZ cameras
PTZ cameras shall be installed at all fuel-feeding/charging points of boilers, thermic fluid heaters, furnaces, kilns and other fuel-fired industrial equipment, as applicable, to facilitate monitoring of fuel usage during operations.
In industrial units using gaseous fuels, PTZ cameras shall be suitably positioned to capture the gas meters/gauges and associated metering arrangements, ensuring adequate visibility for monitoring purposes.
Industrial units shall ensure installation of PTZ cameras for monitoring stack emissions and OCEMS sampling/port-hole locations.
Industrial units shall also ensure installation of PTZ cameras for monitoring fume extraction system areas, wherever applicable.
The number, location and field of view of the cameras shall be adequate to cover the relevant areas and operations effectively, without significant blind spots. Where a single camera cannot adequately cover the prescribed locations, additional cameras shall be installed.
(ii) Real-time video monitoring and connectivity
All PTZ cameras installed pursuant to the Order shall be provided with facilities for continuous, real-time transmission of video feeds through Real Time Streaming Protocol (RTSP) to the designated servers/portals of CPCB and the respective SPCBs/DPCC.
Industrial units shall ensure that the cameras and associated communication systems remain functional and that video feeds are accessible to the concerned regulatory authorities for remote monitoring.
The cameras shall be installed and maintained in a manner that provides adequate image clarity and visibility of the relevant operations, including during night-time operations, wherever applicable.
(iii) Power backup and maintenance
All industrial units shall ensure adequate and uninterrupted power supply, including suitable power backup, for the PTZ cameras, communication equipment and associated connectivity systems.
Industrial units shall be responsible for the proper operation, maintenance and timely restoration of the cameras and connectivity arrangements in the event of any malfunction or disruption.
Any prolonged disruption in video transmission or malfunctioning shall be promptly reported to the concerned SPCB/DPCC, along with the corrective action undertaken.
(iv) Compliance timeline
All industrial units covered under this Order shall ensure installation and operationalization of the requisite PTZ cameras, including arrangements for real-time transmission of video feeds, by 30.11.2026.
CPCB, in coordination with the respective SPCBs/ DPCC, shall ensure necessary technical arrangements, including designated portals, servers and associated infrastructure for receiving and accessing real-time video feeds from industries. The respective SPCBs/ DPCC shall monitor compliance and ensure its effective implementation in their respective jurisdictions.
The respective State Governments of Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan and the GNCTD, along with CPCB and the concerned SPCBs/ DPCC, shall ensure effective implementation of the Order. The requirements under the Order shall be in addition to the existing directions relating to emission standards, use of approved fuels, OCEMS and other pollution-control measures prescribed by the Commission, CPCB and other authorities under applicable environmental laws.
Industrial emissions, including particulate matter (PM) released through stacks and fugitive emissions arising from various industrial processes, contribute significantly to air pollution in the National Capital Region (NCR). Besides directly increasing particulate matter concentrations, and industrial emissions also contribute to the formation of secondary particulate matter, adversely affecting ambient air quality. The impact of such emissions becomes prominent during the winter months, when adverse meteorological conditions restrict the dispersion of pollutants.
The Commission has been undertaking several measures to mitigate industrial air pollution, including transition to cleaner fuels, prohibition of polluting fuels and prescription of stringent emission standards from time to time. The Flying Squads of the Commission, during inspections of industrial units across NCR, have reported instances of use of unapproved fuels, indicating the need for strengthening compliance monitoring and surveillance mechanisms. Accordingly, the monitoring mechanism has been further strengthened with this order.

title: Secretary, Department of Urban Development, MoHUA chairs 10th meeting of CSMC under PMAY-U 2.0
subtitle:
Over 1.93 lakh additional houses approved under the scheme, total houses sanctioned reach 20.80 lakh

Empowering Women, Strengthening Families: 97% of Houses Allotted in Women’s Name or Joint Ownership
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 9:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Over 1.93 lakh additional houses were approved under Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana - Urban 2.0 (PMAY-U 2.0) during the 10th meeting of the Central Sanctioning and Monitoring Committee (CSMC), held in New Delhi on 16th October 2026 under the chairmanship of Shri Satendra Singh, Secretary, Department of Urban Development (DoUD), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA). Shri Kumar Ravikant Singh, Joint Secretary and Mission Director (JS&MD), Housing for All (HFA); Shri Sanjeet, Joint Secretary and Financial Advisor (JS&FA); Shri Vaibhav Rundwal, Director, HFA, officials from the Ministry; and Mission Directors, representatives from the participating 11 States were among those present in the meeting.
With the approval of 1.93 lakh additional houses, the cumulative number of houses sanctioned under the Mission is now at 20.80 lakh. In today’s meeting, houses have been sanctioned under Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC) and Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP) verticals of PMAY-U 2.0 in Andhra Pradesh (6,560 houses), Bihar (52,866 houses), Chhattigarh (4,670 houses), Gujarat (14,290 houses), Karnataka (3,116 houses), Mizoram (1,003 houses), Odisha (3,126 houses), Sikkim (29 houses), Telangana (18,120 houses), Uttar Pradesh (73,182 houses) and West Bengal (16,559 houses) for eligible urban families belonging to the Economically Weaker Section (EWS).
During the meeting, the Committee discussed measures to accelerate the implementation of PMAY-U 2.0, with emphasis on timely approvals, effective monitoring and delivery of housing benefits to eligible beneficiaries.
Expanding Access to Affordable Housing
Launched in September 2024, PMAY-U 2.0 aims to provide financial assistance of up to ₹2.50 lakh each to 1 crore additional urban poor and middle-class families to construct or purchase a pucca house. The scheme extends support to eligible EWS, LIG and MIG families with an annual household income of up to ₹9 lakh.
PMAY-U 2.0 provides assistance through four verticals: Beneficiary Led Construction (BLC), Affordable Housing in Partnership (AHP), Affordable Rental Housing (ARH) and Interest Subsidy Scheme (ISS). The verticals cater to different housing needs of citizens as per their eligibility and requirement.
BLC: Eligible families can construct a pucca house on their own land;
AHP: A beneficiary can purchase their own home in public/private housing projects;
ARH: For those requiring affordable rental accommodation in cities; and
ISS: Interest subsidy of up to ₹1.80 lakh is provided to EWS/LIG and MIG families availing housing loans of up to ₹25 lakh.
Strengthening Implementation through Cooperative Federalism
During the meeting, Secretary, UD underscored the need for close coordination between the Ministry and States/UTs/ULBs to ensure the timely submission and processing of housing proposals. States/UTs were encouraged to address implementation bottlenecks, strengthen project monitoring, identify eligible beneficiaries and expedite the completion and occupancy of houses under approved projects. He further emphasised that the occupancy of already completed AHP houses under PMAY-U should be expedited to ensure that eligible beneficiaries can avail the benefits for their ease of living.
Focus on Timely Approvals and Regular Monitoring
Further, Secretary, UD highlighted the need for regular meetings, timely submission of proposals and sustained monitoring to facilitate effective implementation of the scheme. He stressed that States/UTs must exercise due diligence while preparing and submitting proposals to ensure completeness, accuracy and compliance with prescribed PMAY-U 2.0 guidelines, thereby avoiding delays and procedural hassles.
He directed States/UTs to work closely with the Ministry to resolve implementation-related issues, address matters requiring intervention and ensure that approved projects progress within the prescribed timelines, enabling eligible beneficiaries to receive the intended benefits of the scheme.
Women-Centric and Inclusive Development
PMAY-U 2.0 prioritises women-led development by providing women of the family with ownership or co-ownership of houses. The approach seeks to strengthen women's financial security, improve their role in household decision-making and provide families with a stronger foundation for long-term stability.
The Mission also seeks to extend the benefits of affordable housing to eligible families from vulnerable and underserved sections of urban society. By facilitating access to formal housing, the scheme contributes to improved living conditions and supports the social and economic well-being of beneficiary households.
Of the 20.80 lakh houses sanctioned under PMAY-U 2.0, 20.16 lakh houses (97%) have been allotted to women (ownership or joint ownership).
Further, to promote inclusivity, 1.81 lakh houses have been sanctioned to senior citizens; 3.61 lakh houses for SC beneficiaries, 1.06 lakh for ST beneficiaries and 9.14 lakh for OBC beneficiaries, reaffirming the scheme’s commitment to equitable access to safe, affordable and dignified housing.
Towards the Goal of ‘Housing for All’
The approval of 20.80 lakh houses under PMAY-U 2.0 represents continued progress towards the Mission's objective of extending affordable housing support to eligible urban families. Overall, under PMAY-U and PMAY-U 2.0, more than 1.27 crore houses have been sanctioned by the Government while 1.01 crore houses are already completed.
PMAY-U 2.0 continues to turn the vision of ‘Housing for All’ into reality, bringing millions of urban families closer to a secure home, a dignified life and a brighter future.

title: Shri Manoj Goel, Chairman, KVIC inaugurated ‘Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ in Mumbai with the aim of taking Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call of ‘Har Ghar Swadeshi, Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi’ to Gen-Z through the ‘Baat Khadi Ki’ podcast
subtitle:
The exhibition features 77 units from 12 states across the country showcasing a diverse range of Khadi and village industry products

“Youth entrepreneurship, contemporary fashion and digital markets can give Khadi a new identity in the journey from Local to Global”: KVIC Chairman
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 2:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Shri Manoj Goel, Chairman, Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, Government of India inaugurated ‘Khadi Mahotsav-2026’ on Thursday, 15th October 2026, at the KVIC Central Office in Vile Parle, Mumbai. Organised with the objective to take Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s call of “Har Ghar Swadeshi, Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi” and “Vocal for Local” to the younger generation, particularly Gen Z, the festival provides an important platform for connecting Khadi and Village Industries products with modern lifestyles and creating new markets for the country’s artisans and rural entrepreneurs. Senior KVIC officials and staff including the CEO, Financial Advisor, Joint CEO, CVO and Deputy CEOs along with representatives of Khadi institutions and artisans and entrepreneurs associated with PMEGP and village industry development, were present at the event.
The Khadi Mahotsav,  organised  from 2 October to 31 October 2026, provides a special discount of 20% on Khadi products and 10% on Village Industries products. A total of 77 units from 12 states are displaying and selling their products through 77 stalls. These include 36 Khadi units, 33 units associated with PMEGP, and 08 units of  Village Industries and other schemes. Participating states include Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, West Bengal, Haryana, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra and Rajasthan. The exhibition features a wide range of indigenous products including Khadi fabrics, silk Khadi, poly-Khadi, ready-made garments, herbal products, food items, soaps, incense sticks, spices, leather products, artificial jewellery, wooden toys, bags, Phulkari, amla-based products and wooden handicrafts.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Manoj Goel, Chairman, KVIC said that the Father of the Nation, Mahatma Gandhi, had made Khadi a symbol of self-reliance and economic self-sufficiency during the freedom movement. Today, it is the need of the hour to take Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi's call for “Swadeshi” to the new generation. He further said that the younger generation has a special association with Khadi. The energy, creativity, technological understanding and entrepreneurial spirit of Gen Z can play an important role in connecting the Swadeshi movement with wider public participation. He further stated that the Prime Minister's message of ‘Har Ghar Swadeshi, Ghar-Ghar Swadeshi’ (Swadeshi in every home) is not limited merely to the purchase of indigenous goods. Its broader objective is to foster a sense of pride in Indian products, encourage local producers, and strengthen the country's economic self-reliance. The participation of the youth holds special significance in this campaign, as they can give indigenous products a new identity in society through their choices, lifestyles, digital platforms, and entrepreneurial initiatives.
Shri Goel stated that today's Gen-Z is conscious of fashion, design, technology, and new ideas. Khadi can be made more popular among young people by integrating it with contemporary designs, attractive garments, improved branding and modern lifestyles. Khadi’s natural identity, Indian heritage and association with sustainable living make it a meaningful choice for the younger generation.
He stated that the need of the hour is to adapt Khadi’s presentation and marketing to changing times while preserving its traditional essence. Young people can become not only consumers of indigenous products but also their brand ambassadors, designers, digital promoters and entrepreneurs. Through social media, e-commerce, digital marketing, and startups, the youth can take Khadi and village industry products to every corner of the country and also connect them to international markets.
He further stated that KVIC has launched the ‘Baat Khadi Ki’ podcast with the aim of taking Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s vision of ‘Viksit Bharat@2047’ and ‘Vocal for Local’ to the younger generation. This podcast initiative seeks to connect Gen-Z with the “Swadeshi” movement through conversations with emphasis  on Khadi’s heritage, innovation, modern fashion, and youth entrepreneurship. This initiative will help to align Khadi with the preferences and modern lifestyles of the younger generation while advancing the Prime Minister’s vision of an Aatmanirbhar Bharat.
The KVIC Chairman stated that taking forward Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s message of ‘Local to Global’ and securing global recognition for local products presents a significant opportunity for the Khadi and Village Industries sector. To achieve this, special consideration must be  given to product quality, contemporary design, attractive packaging, effective branding and access to digital marketplaces. He added that Gen Z can become a key partner in this transformation. Young designers can integrate Khadi with contemporary fashion, digital entrepreneurs can expand its markets, and start-ups can develop new business models for traditional products. This will provide wider markets for the skills of local artisans and create opportunities for Indian products to establish their identity internationally.
Speaking to the media, Chairman KVIC Shri Manoj Goel reiterated that the Khadi and Village Industries sector has achieved unprecedented progress as a result of the visionary approach and policies of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. During the year 2025-26, the turnover of the Khadi and Village Industries sector surpassed ₹1.87 lakh crore, while the sector is providing employment to over 2.04 crore people.
He assured that the sector would achieve its turnover target of ₹2.51 lakh crore in the coming years.

The two-day National Conference on e-Governance Reforms kick-started today in Dharamshala, Himachal Pradesh, bringing together representatives of the Central, State/UT Governments and experts to deliberate on digital transformation, innovative governance practices and technology-enabled public service delivery.
The inaugural session featured a welcome address by Smt. Nivedita Shukla Verma, Secretary, DARPG, Government of India, followed by addresses by Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pant, Chief Secretary, Government of Himachal Pradesh, and Shri Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh. Shri Puneet Yadav, Additional Secretary, DARPG, delivered the vote of thanks.
In his address, the Chief Minister said, the reforms must be brought about to ensure the welfare of the beneficiaries and modern technology can prove to be a key instrument in addressing the future challenges. He said that the state Government was focusing on good governance and the departments must make earnest efforts to provide quality services to the people of the State nearer to their homes. He applauded Union Minister of State (PP) Dr Jitendra Singh and DARPG for organising the conference in Himachal Pradesh.
Citing
nominations received under National Awards for e-Governance and the Prime Minister's Awards, Secretary DARPG in her address highlighted the innovative work done by Districts, States and Ministries to make governance more robust and citizen centric. She underlined that the challenge before the government was to scale up such practices and to take an innovation that works in one place and make it work in many places. She emphasized that closing the distance between a successful pilot and a national practice was the objective of the National Conference.
Expressing gratitude to the Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh and the state administration for their support and hospitality in hosting the conference, the Secretary noted the visionary leadership and continuous guidance provided by Union Minister of State (PP) Dr. Jitendra Singh in driving DARPG’s governance initiatives. Acknowledgment was also extended to Union Minister for Health Shri J. P. Nadda. Both the ministers have  conveyed their best wishes for the National Conference.
Chief Secretary of Government of Himachal Pradesh, Shri Kamlesh Kumar Pant highlighted how e-governance is enabling citizens to access government services at their doorsteps. He outlined various initiatives undertaken by the Himachal Pradesh government and explained how digital governance is helping reduce procedural hurdles. He emphasised that the objective is to eliminate barriers, promote equality and ensure that public services reach people more efficiently.
The session brought together senior leadership from the Central and State Governments for deliberations on governance reforms and the role of digital innovation in public administration.
The Day One of the Conference showcased five key initiatives of the Government of Himachal Pradesh, including Him Parivar, Sukhashraya, Vidya Samiksha Kendra (VSK), Green Himachal and the Rajiv Gandhi Van Samvardhan Yojna. The presentations highlighted the range of governance initiatives being undertaken across sectors such as health, social justice, education, environment and forest conservation.
The other sessions featured presentations on award-recognised initiatives demonstrating the use of digital platforms, artificial intelligence and emerging technologies in governance. The initiatives included AgriStack, e-Jagriti, the AI-enabled Clinical Decision Support System in e-Sanjeevani Telemedicine Service, the Multi Hazard Early Warning Decision Support System and iGOT Karmayogi. The presentations wer  also made on eAarogya Dhamni, the District Court Case Management System (DCMS), ICMR-MINDS, the India Hypertension Control Initiative and Digi Yatra.
Day Two of the conference, scheduled for 17 October 2026, will feature sessions on cybersecurity, best e-governance practices, replication, data analytics, and State-, district- and grassroots-level initiatives, followed by the valedictory session.
The National Conference on e-Governance Reforms seeks to strengthen the exchange of ideas and experiences among government institutions and promote effective, innovative and citizen-centric governance through digital transformation.

title: NHAI Successfully Defends Arbitration Case in Chittorgarh–Udaipur National Highway Project to Safeguard Public Funds
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 5:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Achieving a significant legal
victory,
NHAI has successfully defended its contractual position in an arbitration case against concessionaire Uchit Expressway Private Limited, promoted by TRIL Roads Pvt. Ltd. for six-laning of the 93.5 km long Chittorgarh-Udaipur section of NH-76 in Rajasthan. The Arbitral Tribunal substantially upheld the position of NHAI, thereby safeguarding public resources and reaffirming the contractual framework governing National Highway projects.
The three-member Arbitral Tribunal under the Society for Affordable Redressal of Disputes (SAROD), examined claims and counterclaims arising out of the concession agreement for the project. The Tribunal rejected overall concessionaire claims of Rs. 366.53 crores, which included Rs. 238.18 crore of prolongation cost claim tied to COVID-19 by the concessionaire. After detailed consideration, the Tribunal rejected the claim for prolongation cost and allowed claims amounting to only Rs. 14.51 crore along with conditional refund of Rs. 2.82 Crores to the concessionaire.
In addition, the Tribunal awarded Rs. 33.54 crore (principal) in counter-claims to NHAI. This ruling in favour of NHAI includes Rs. 27 crore for recovery of work dropped from the project scope, Rs. 4.03 crore toward failure to maintain the highway and Rs. 2.51 crore towards unauthorized toll collected after the completion date of the project, in March 2021.
In a series of recent notable legal wins, NHAI has successfully defended various arbitration cases. In July 2026, NHAI successfully defended claims of around Rs. 3,177 crores in the arbitration proceedings pertaining to Bareilly Highways Project Limited (BHPL).Similarly, in June 2026, arbitration case related to Tumkur–Chitradurga 6 laning Project in Karnataka, was awarded in favour of NHAI for Rs. 1,202 crores. Also in April 2026, two arbitration cases in Panipat–Jalandhar Highway Project involving Concessionaire’s claims of around Rs. 8,375 Crores and counterclaims of NHAI for Rs. 2,888.64 Crores were settled for Rs. 819.96 Crores in favour of NHAI. Similarly in May 2026, arbitration case related to 6 laning of Kamrej–Chalthan section of NH-48 in Gujarat in which claims of around Rs. 174.49 crore raised by the contractor, was settled for only Rs. 54 lakhs by the Arbitral Tribunal.
The successful resolution of arbitration cases reflects NHAI’s commitment to sound contractual management and effective legal strategy. It also reaffirms NHAI’s focus on the proper utilization of public funds, while upholding transparency, accountability and contractual discipline in the development and management of National Highway infrastructure.

title: Climate history finds monsoon fluctuation footprints from sediment transport to farming adaptations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 3:42PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A new study has found that Indian Summer Monsoon fluctuations have, through the years, controlled lake hydrology, sediment transport, vegetation, sedimentary organic matter, microbial activity, and early farming adaptation in the Central Ganga Plain.
This could help strengthen climate and agricultural adaptation, guide water security and wetland conservation, enhance disaster risk reduction and advance understanding of human-climate interactions.
Scientists have been trying to address the long-standing question of how past climatic extremes influenced the evolution of human societies in the Indian subcontinent. The rise and decline of the Indus Valley Civilization have been widely linked to changes in the Indian Summer Monsoon. However, much less is known about how later communities in the Central Ganga Plain responded to similar climatic fluctuations. As one of the major centres of agricultural expansion and cultural development after the decline of the Indus Valley Civilization, the Ganga Plain provides an ideal natural laboratory to investigate long-term climate–human interactions, as multiple migrations have been recorded during 4500-1000 cal yr BP in this region.
Scientists from Birbal Sahni Institute of Palaeosciences (BSIP), an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), reconstructed 4600 years of climate and environmental history by tracing palaeo-environmental conditions using proxies such as stable isotopes, vegetation changes as well as archaeological and sedimentary records from Karela Lake, an oxbow lake in Hulas Khera near Lucknow in the Central Ganga Plain.
Fig. 1.
(A) Study area map of the Hulas-Khera (KLT) lake, Mohanlal Ganj, Lucknow, showing the location of the lake within Uttar Pradesh. (B) Present-day view of the study site. (C) Location of the Hulas-Khera archaeological site (Kushan settlement) in close proximity to the lake. (D) Mean monthly precipitation (1901 to 2020 AD) for the Hulas-Khera region, extracted from the KNMI Climatic explorer (
https://climexp.knmi.nl/start.cgi
)
.
Sediments of the lake preserve a record of Late Holocene environmental changes. Besides, the lake's proximity to the Hulas Khera archaeological site provided opportunity to investigate how ancient agricultural communities responded to changing climatic conditions.
The study helped restructure records of hydrology, sedimentary processes, vegetation dynamics, and manure-based agricultural practices with herbivore records. Moisture records during the Little Ice Age (LIA) through westerly winds further clarified the imprints of flooding in the region during the colder phase of the LIA.
The researchers also integrated AMS-based radiocarbon chronology, stable isotopes of C and N, grain-size analysis, end-member modelling, and palynology for a more comprehensive and reliable reconstruction of climate, vegetation dynamics, hydrogeological history, and human activities than previously achieved.
Fig. 2.
Schematic view of the Karela lake (Hulas Khera) showing the climatic events and overall view of the study.
Biswajeet Thakur, Anand Rajoriya, Maneesha M ET and the radiocarbon dating laboratory team identified four major environmental phases associated with key climatic events, including the 4.2 ka arid event, the Roman Warm Period, and the Little Ice Age.
The study published in the Journal of Asian Earth Sciences integrated
geochemical, isotopic, sedimentological, and biological evidence within a robust AMS radiocarbon chronology to decipher complex climate–ecosystem interactions.
It demonstrated that fluctuations in the Indian Summer Monsoon not only regulated lake hydrology, sediment transport, and shifts between C₃ and C₄ vegetation but also influenced the composition of sedimentary organic matter, its deposition pattern, microbial activities and the adaptive strategies developed by early agricultural communities in the Central Ganga Plain.
The study also established that small oxbow lakes of the Central Ganga Plain are highly sensitive natural archives capable of preserving long-term monsoon records, ecosystem evolution, and human-environment interactions, thereby providing an important baseline for understanding future environmental change in one of India's most densely populated and agriculturally important regions.
This could advance understanding of climate–human interactions and help support national climate and environmental policies by generating long-term baseline datasets essential for climate modelling, ecosystem management, land-use planning, and implementation of national priorities on climate adaptation, food security, water security, and sustainable development.

title: Indian scientists identify a few Martian analogue sites
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 3:39PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Two key minerals identified in areas of Tamil Nadu and the Atacama Desert in Chile, which reflect geological, chemical, and physical similarities with Mars, have helped establish these as Martian analogue sites.
In the era of intense planetary exploration, identifying terrestrial analogue sites has become a pressing requirement, as recent studies demonstrate that orbital data alone cannot fully characterize Martian minerals. High-precision, state-of-the-art analytical tools are essential for these investigations.
Advanced instrumentation, including a laser Raman spectrometer, supported by the DST-FIST at the Department of Geology, University of Kerala, has helped identify melanterite in Neyveli, Tamil Nadu, and Gypsum in the Atacama Desert (Chile) and the Tiruchirappalli Badlands, a semi-arid geological and paleoclimatic terrain in Tamil Nadu. Both minerals are hydrous sulphates that record water–rock interactions. While gypsum preserves evidence of past aqueous environments, melanterite indicates transient wet, acidic, and oxidizing conditions, processes relevant to those inferred on Mars.
Fig 1
: Stage-wise depiction of the formation of melanterite from marcasite from the lignite substratum of Neyveli
The identification was carried out by the research team from the University of Kerala, led by Dr. Sajin Kumar K.S., Project Coordinator, DST-FIST. The DST-FIST-supported Laser Raman Spectrometer was used to detect the distinctive spectral fingerprints of the minerals and confirm their identification. Melanterite provides evidence for short-lived wet conditions through sulphide oxidation, a process relevant to sulphate formation on Mars, while gypsum records past aqueous activity and can preserve biosignatures within its mineral matrix. Thus, these terrestrial minerals provide useful analogues for understanding past water activity and potentially habitable environments on Mars.
These findings have been published as two research papers in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Planets, a leading journal on planetary science.
Fig 2
: Schematic illustration of gypsum formation sequences in the two terrestrial analog sites (a) Atacama Desert (b) Tiruchirappalli Badlands
The team is now focusing on rare analogue sites in extreme conditions across different parts of the globe to understand primitive life for astrobiological studies, using the same facility.
Such facilities supported by the DST-FIST can advance planetary science by improving our understanding of past habitable environments on Mars and other planetary bodies. Identifying minerals capable of recording water activity and preserving biosignatures can also help guide future planetary missions toward the most promising locations in the search for evidence of life beyond Earth.
Fig 3
: The laser Raman instrument facility at the Department of Geology, which is funded by the DST-FIST

title: TDB-DST signs agreement with QNu Labs for ₹150 crore RDI support to strengthen India’s indigenous quantum-secure technology ecosystem
subtitle: Project to advance a sovereign technology stack for India’s Quantum Secure and Sensing Networks, targeting TRL-9
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 2:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a significant step towards strengthening India’s capabilities in quantum technologies and secure communications, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with QNu Labs Private Limited, Bengaluru, Karnataka for financial support of ₹150 crore under the Research Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund.
The project, with a total cost of ₹300 crore, aims to develop an indigenous technology backbone for India’s Quantum Secure and Sensing Networks (IQSN). The programme will advance a portfolio of technologies from Technology Readiness Levels (TRL) 4–5 towards TRL-9, supporting the development, integration and validation of a sovereign quantum-security and sensing technology stack. The financial support will be provided through Optionally Convertible Debt (OCD).
As digital infrastructure becomes increasingly interconnected, securing the authenticity of devices, the integrity of navigation systems, the reliability of time synchronisation and the confidentiality of communications is emerging as a critical technological priority. Quantum technologies offer new approaches to addressing these challenges, particularly in applications where conventional security mechanisms may face limitations from evolving cyber and technological threats. QNu Labs’ proposed programme seeks to address these requirements through an integrated framework built around four pillars: identity security, location integrity, network security and time integrity. The programme brings together complementary capabilities to establish a unified foundation for sovereign security and sensing infrastructure.
Under the identity security pillar, the programme envisages quantum-secure physical unclonable functions (PUFs) and quantum-safe trusted platform modules (TPMs) to support hardware-based device identity, authentication and cryptographic security. These technologies are intended to strengthen trust at the device level and reduce vulnerabilities associated with compromised or replicated identities. The location integrity pillar focuses on technologies designed to support trusted navigation and detect attempts to manipulate or spoof positioning systems. The proposed work includes compact quantum magnetometers for electromagnetic tampering detection and GPS-denied navigation capabilities, with potential applications in defence and other mission-critical platforms.
Under network security, the programme seeks to advance a quantum-secure communications ecosystem through chip-based quantum key distribution (QKD), satellite-based QKD and supporting technologies such as quantum-secure communication modules and encryption systems. The objective is to develop deployable capabilities for secure communications across terrestrial and long-distance networks.
The fourth pillar, time integrity, focuses on indigenous high-precision timing infrastructure, including atomic clock technology and secure time synchronisation using QKD-authenticated distribution. Reliable and tamper-resistant time synchronisation is essential for telecommunications, financial systems, critical infrastructure and defence applications. Together, these four pillars are intended to contribute to an integrated quantum trust framework supporting device authenticity, secure communications, trusted navigation and tamper-resistant timing. The programme will involve further research, engineering refinement, system integration and validation to progress the technologies towards higher levels of readiness and deployment.
Shri Rajesh Kumar Pathak, Secretary, TDB, said:
“Quantum technologies are opening new possibilities for addressing complex challenges in cybersecurity, communications, navigation and critical infrastructure. Building indigenous capabilities across these interconnected domains is important for strengthening India’s technological self-reliance and long-term security. Through the RDI Fund, TDB is supporting the development and maturation of advanced technologies that require sustained investment to progress from research and engineering to integrated, deployable systems.”
Founder of QNu Labs Private Limited said:
“Quantum technologies will shape how nations protect their communications, devices, navigation and timing systems. TDB’s support under the RDI Fund allows us to accelerate our R&D roadmap beyond quantum security stack. Our work will focus on four connected areas: device identity, location integrity, network security and time integrity, so that trust is built into infrastructure from the hardware upwards. This programme extends quantum security foundation into chip-based and satellite-based QKD, quantum sensing and AI. We see this partnership as a responsibility: to deliver indigenous capabilities that India’s defence, telecom, financial and critical infrastructure sectors can rely on, and to strengthen the wider quantum ecosystem through collaboration with academia, startups and industry.”

title: National Steering Committee Approves ₹1,194.92 Crore Investment Under PM-SETU for Five ITI Clusters Across Maharashtra, Odisha and Jammu & Kashmir
subtitle: Tata Steel Foundation, BVG India, Belrise Industries, Eagle Infra India and Inderdeep Infra India to partner in upgrading five ITI clusters; cumulative investment approved under PM-SETU reaches ₹3,687 crore
ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 3:25PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 6th National Steering Committee (NSC) meeting of the Pradhan Mantri Skilling and Employability Transformation through Upgraded ITIs (PM-SETU) was held today under the chairpersonship of Smt. Debashree Mukherjee, Secretary, Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE). The Committee reviewed the progress of the scheme and approved five Strategic Investment Plans (SIPs) worth ₹1,194.92 crore for ITI clusters across Maharashtra, Odisha and Jammu & Kashmir.
With these approvals, the cumulative investment approved under PM-SETU has reached ₹3,687 crore till date, marking another significant milestone in the Government of India's efforts to transform Industrial Training Institutes (ITIs) into modern, industry-aligned and future-ready skill institutions.
The meeting was attended by senior officials from the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE), including Shri Niranjan Kumar Sudhanshu, Additional Secretary, MSDE, and Smt. Manasi Sahay Thakur, Joint Secretary, MSDE, along with representatives from the Directorate General of Training (DGT), State Governments and Union Territories, industry partners, multilateral development banks (MDBs), and other stakeholders associated with the implementation of PM-SETU.
Charing the meeting Ms. Debashree Mukherjee Secretary MSDE said, “The approvals given by the National Steering Committee are an important step in implementing PM-SETU. They will help strengthen ITIs, improve training and increase industry participation. We encourage clusters to work towards ISO certification and include at least one WorldSkills-aligned trade or competency area in their Approved Implementation Plans. Our aim is to improve training quality and help young people gain skills that lead to better employment opportunities. The progress made by Jammu & Kashmir is encouraging and reflects a strong commitment to strengthening skilling and expanding opportunities for youth in the region.”
The approved Strategic Investment Plans will be implemented through partnerships between State Governments, industry partners and participating ITIs under the PM-SETU framework. The projects will focus on modernising infrastructure, introducing industry-aligned courses, strengthening trainer capacity, enhancing industry engagement and improving employability outcomes for youth.
The approved clusters are as follows:
Kataka ITI Cluster in Odisha to be Upgraded in Partnership with Tata Steel Foundation
The National Steering Committee approved a Strategic Investment Plan worth ₹240.50 crore for the Kataka ITI Cluster in Odisha in partnership with Tata Steel Foundation.
The cluster comprises Government ITI Kataka as the Hub and Madhusudan Government ITI Choudwar, Government ITI Paradeep, Government ITI Jajpur and Government ITI Dhenkanal as Spokes.
The project aims to strengthen infrastructure, introduce new-age training programmes and enhance industry linkages to meet the emerging skill requirements of the region.
Pune ITI Cluster to be Upgraded in Partnership with BVG India
The National Steering Committee approved a Strategic Investment Plan worth ₹241 crore for the Pune ITI Cluster in Maharashtra to be implemented by BVG India Limited, in consortium with BVG Foundation.
The cluster comprises Government ITI Aundh, Pune as the Hub and Government ITI Aundh (Women), Government ITI Pimpri Chinchwad, Government ITI Khed (Rajgurunagar) and Government ITI Mulshi as Spokes.
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar ITI Cluster to be Upgraded in Partnership with Belrise Industries
The Committee approved a Strategic Investment Plan worth ₹238.01 crore for the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar ITI Cluster in Maharashtra in partnership with Belrise Industries Limited.
The cluster comprises Government ITI Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar as the Hub and Government ITI Paithan, Government ITI Khultabad, Government ITI Phulambri and Government ITI Gangapur as Spokes.
Jammu ITI Cluster to be Upgraded in Partnership with Eagle Infra India
The Committee approved a Strategic Investment Plan worth ₹240 crore for the Jammu ITI Cluster in the Union Territory of Jammu & Kashmir in partnership with Eagle Infra India Limited.
The cluster comprises Government ITI Jammu as the Hub and Government ITI R.S. Pura, Government ITI Nowshera, Government ITI Samba and Government ITI Kathua as Spokes.
Srinagar ITI Cluster to be Upgraded in Partnership with Inderdeep Infra India
The National Steering Committee also approved a Strategic Investment Plan worth ₹235.41 crore for the Srinagar ITI Cluster in Jammu & Kashmir in partnership with Inderdeep Infra India Limited.
The cluster comprises Government ITI Srinagar as the Hub and Government ITI Ganderbal, Government ITI Kangan, Government ITI Budgam and Government ITI Charar-i-Sharief as Spokes.
Progress under PM-SETU Training of Trainers under Component II Reviewed
The National Steering Committee reviewed progress under the Training of Trainers (ToT) under component II of PM-SETU scheme, which aims to build a robust pool of industry-ready instructors equipped with contemporary technical and pedagogical competencies.
As of October 2026, 3,744 trainers have been trained under the programme through National Skill Training Institutes (NSTIs).
