title: PM-AJAY Drives Inclusive Development Through Adarsh Grams, Socio-Economic Projects and Educational Infrastructure
subtitle:
18,093 villages declared Adarsh Grams; Approximately Rs 1,730 Crore released under Grant In Aid directly to States And Districts

785 student hostels completed; Rs 61.46 Crore Allocated For FY 2026-27 for two hostel projects Accommodating 264 Boys/ Girls Students
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 6:26PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Under the Adarsh Gram component of Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, over 47,200 villages benefiting more than 47.79 lakh citizens across the country, have been covered. In addition, a total of 46,944 development works have been completed, while 27,032 Village Development Plans (VDPs) have been prepared, under the PM AJAY.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said as on September 8, 2026, 18,093 villages had been declared Adarsh Grams which reflects continued efforts of the Ministry to improve infrastructure, basic services and the quality of life in Scheduled Caste-majority villages.
He said the Scheduled Caste-dominated villages are being developed as model villages by addressing critical gaps in infrastructure and essential services and an ‘Adarsh Gram’ is envisioned as a village where people have access to basic services, the minimum needs of all sections of society are met and disparities are reduced to a minimum.
The Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) implemented by the Ministry, is advancing the socio-economic and educational empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities through infrastructure development, livelihood promotion, education and improved access to basic services.
The Official informed that the Scheme has three components including development of Scheduled Caste-dominated villages into ‘Adarsh Grams’, Grants-in-Aid for socio-economic projects at the State and District levels, and construction and repair of hostels.
He stated that the Grants-in-Aid component provides financial assistance for district and State-level projects aimed at the socio-economic advancement of Scheduled Castes. It focuses on increasing the income of the target population through comprehensive livelihood projects, skill development and related infrastructure, he added.
He said it also seeks to improve socio-economic development indicators by creating adequate infrastructure in Scheduled Caste-dominated villages and to promote literacy and school enrolment among Scheduled Caste students through residential schools wherever required.
The Official said an approximately Rs 1,730 Crore was released directly to States under this component during FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26. The support has extended skilling and livelihood opportunities to more than 2.5 lakh individual and group beneficiaries, he added.
The Official further said under the PM-AJAY’s component of construction and repair of hostels, the Ministry pursues enabling and encouraging Scheduled Caste students to pursue quality education as these hostels are particularly beneficial for students from rural and remote areas by providing access to accommodation and educational opportunities.
He said as of September 2026, a total of 785 student hostels had been completed under the scheme. For FY 2026-27, the Government has allocated Rs 61.46 crore in central assistance for two hostel projects—one for girls and one for boys—which will provide accommodation for 264 students, he further said.
The Ministry Official further said a major step towards strengthening implementation and monitoring has been the launch of the PM-AJAY Mobile App and PM-AJAY Portal, facilitating a transition from paper-based workflows to end-to-end digital processing on a real-time basis.
He said technology-enabled governance is strengthening information access, monitoring and data-driven decision-making under the scheme while as the digital framework is also aimed at improving coordination, transparency, accountability and efficiency in the delivery of welfare interventions.
The Official further stated that PM-AJAY is a 100 per cent Centrally Funded Scheme, while States and Union Territories may supplement it with additional resources wherever required. Under the funding framework, up to 50 per cent of funds may be utilised for gap-filling activities in selected Adarsh Gram villages. Up to 5 per cent is allocated for setting up and operating Technical Support Groups and Project Implementation Units at the Central, State and District levels. Up to 2 per cent is earmarked for construction and repair of hostels, including support for Central Institutions, while the remaining funds are provided as Grants-in-Aid for projects at the District and State levels.
Grants-in-Aid allocations take into account factors including the Scheduled Caste population and the ratio of State SCSP to the Annual Plan in relation to the Scheduled Caste population of States and Union Territories. Following completion of infrastructure projects, their maintenance and operation are to be undertaken by the concerned State Governments or implementing agencies. Under the hostel component, the Government of India also provides central assistance for maintenance.
As India progresses towards Viksit Bharat @2047, ensuring that the benefits of development reach every section of society remains central to the nation’s development journey.
PM-AJAY contributes to this objective by addressing multiple dimensions of empowerment—from village infrastructure and basic services to livelihoods, skill development and access to education.
With greater use of technology, stronger monitoring mechanisms and focused last-mile delivery, the scheme continues to strengthen opportunities for Scheduled Caste communities to participate more fully in India’s growth and development. Its integrated approach is helping create the infrastructure, capabilities and enabling environment required for individuals and communities to realise their full potential.

title: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment Organises Lecture on Records Management under Special Campaign 6.0
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 4:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Department of Social Justice and Empowerment (DoSJE), Government of India, organised a lecture on Records Management at the Samvaad Conference Room, at the Ministry in National Capital here. The programme was a part of Special Campaign 6 for
Institutionalizing Swachhata and Minimizing Pendency.
Shri P. K. Jaiswal, Former Faculty Member, Institute of Secretariat Training and Management (ISTM), delivered the lecture.
A Senior Official in the Ministry said the session focused on sensitizing departmental officials to the importance of systematic records management, proper maintenance and preservation of official records, timely review of files, and adherence to prescribed procedures for record retention and weeding out.
During the session, participants were apprised of the relevant provisions of the Public Records Act, the Record Retention Schedule, the categorisation of records, and departmental instructions governing their retention and disposal. The lecture emphasised the need for systematic record keeping and compliance with established procedures to ensure the effective management of official documents.
The Official further said the session also highlighted how efficient records management contributes to better utilisation of office space, easy retrieval of official information and improved administrative efficiency. Effective management of both physical and electronic records plays an important role in strengthening transparency, accountability and timely decision-making in government functioning, he added.
The lecture forms part of the Department’s ongoing initiatives under
Special Campaign 6.0
to promote cleanliness in office premises, streamline record rooms, minimise pendency and institutionalise efficient office management practices.
Through such initiatives, the Department of Social Justice and Empowerment continues to promote a clean, organised and responsive working environment while strengthening administrative efficiency in line with the objectives of
Special Campaign 6.0

title: From Addiction to Recovery
subtitle: Asha Ram’s Journey Towards Renewed Hope and Social Reintegration
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 3:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Mr. Ramesh Kumar’s
(name changed)
experience demonstrates how timely intervention and compassionate rehabilitation can help individuals move beyond addiction and work towards a healthier, more dignified future.
Through support under NAPDDR at the Saidhantik Drug De-Addiction Center, Mandla, Madhya Pradesh, he has taken meaningful steps towards renewed hope, improved well-being and social reintegration. His story reflects the importance of inclusive services that support recovery and help individuals reconnect with their families and communities.
At the age of 55, Mr. Ramesh Kumar
,
a resident of Mandla district, Madhya Pradesh, faced significant challenges due to long-term substance abuse. Belonging to the Scheduled Caste community and having studied up to middle school, he was unemployed and experienced a decline in his physical and mental well-being, financial stability and family relationships. His struggles included depression, social isolation and difficulties in meeting basic needs.
Substance dependence affected his concentration and memory and made it difficult for him to regain control over his daily life. Financial resources were frequently spent on substances, resulting in further economic hardship. Stigma and discrimination associated with addiction added to his difficulties and discouraged him from seeking timely assistance. Strained family relationships and social exclusion further intensified these challenges.
A turning point came when he received support at the Saidhantik Drug De-Addiction Center, operated by Saidhantik Shiksha Samiti in Mandla, Madhya Pradesh, under the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction (NAPDDR). On 7 May 2026, he began receiving comprehensive assistance to address the medical, psychological, emotional and social dimensions of substance dependence.
The Centre provided free and structured support, including medical detoxification, individual counselling, cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT), family therapy, rehabilitation activities and safe shelter during recovery. Through counselling and therapeutic interventions, he received guidance to understand the effects of substance dependence, manage emotional distress and develop healthier coping mechanisms.
Family counselling and education helped strengthen mutual understanding and encouraged a supportive environment for his recovery. Group therapy and relapse-prevention training helped him rebuild confidence, develop essential life skills and prepare to manage situations that could threaten his progress. This integrated approach supported not only his treatment but also his emotional well-being, family relationships and social reintegration.
With support from the centre, Mr. Ramesh Kumar has made encouraging progress towards recovery. His physical and mental well-being have improved, and he has regained greater emotional stability and confidence. His family relationships have also improved, helping him move towards a more stable and socially connected life.
Although he remains unemployed, the recovery process has helped him regain confidence and prepare for future livelihood opportunities. His journey highlights the importance of accessible de-addiction services, professional counselling, family participation and sustained rehabilitation in helping individuals overcome substance dependence and rebuild their lives.

title: From Contractual Sanitation Worker to Entrepreneur: Sanjay Kumar’s Journey Towards Financial Independence Under NAMASTE
subtitle: A Sanitation Worker from Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, Builds an Independent Livelihood Through Mechanised Sanitation Services
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Mr. Sanjay Kumar’s journey highlights how access to institutional credit and capital subsidy can help sanitation workers transition towards mechanised sanitation, entrepreneurship and improved livelihood opportunities. By enabling him to own and operate a desludging vehicle, the support under SUY has helped him establish an independent source of income while contributing to the adoption of mechanised sanitation services.
Mr. Sanjay Kumar, a 42-year-old resident of Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh, faced financial challenges while supporting his family of six. Employed as a contractual sanitation worker, he earned approximately ₹12,000 per month.
Despite his hard work and dedication, his modest income made it difficult to meet household expenses, fulfil his family’s needs and build financial security for the future.
Having completed middle school, Mr. Kumar had limited employment opportunities and few prospects for increasing his earnings. As the sole earning member of his family, he aspired to improve his financial circumstances and provide a better standard of living for his loved ones. His ambition was to own a mechanised cleaning vehicle and establish an independent sanitation services business.
A significant opportunity emerged when Mr. Kumar attended an awareness camp organised at the Ghaziabad Municipal Corporation. During the camp, he learned about the
Swachhta Udyami Yojana (SUY)
under the
National Action for Mechanised Sanitation Ecosystem (NAMASTE) Scheme
, implemented by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India.
Through the scheme, he received an upfront capital subsidy from the Ministry and a loan from Canara Bank to procure a desludging vehicle. The total project cost was ₹9.55 lakh, comprising a loan of ₹5.91 lakh and a capital subsidy of ₹3.64 lakh. The financial assistance, received during 2021–22, enabled him to acquire the vehicle and transition from contractual employment to self-employment as a mechanised sanitation service provider.
The intervention marked a turning point in Mr. Kumar’s livelihood. From earning ₹12,000 per month as a contractual worker, he now earns approximately ₹60,000–₹65,000 per month through his sanitation services business. After meeting operational expenses, he is able to save around ₹25,000 every month. This improvement has strengthened his family’s financial stability and enabled him to plan better for future needs.
Today, Mr. Sanjay Kumar’s experience demonstrates how targeted financial assistance can create opportunities for economic empowerment. His journey from a contractual sanitation worker to an entrepreneur reflects the potential of the NAMASTE Scheme to promote self-employment, strengthen financial independence and improve the quality of life of sanitation workers and their families.

title: NFSC Fellowship Empowers Ajay Kumar to Pursue His PhD
subtitle: A Scholar from Kangra, Himachal Pradesh Advances His Academic Aspirations
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 1:54PM by PIB Delhi
content:
A Scholar from Kangra Himachal Pradesh, Ajay Kumar’s journey reflects the determination of students who continue to pursue higher education despite financial challenges.
Ajay Kumar, a 33-year-old scholar is pursuing his Ph.D. with the aspiration of achieving academic excellence, building a successful career and improving his socio-economic circumstances.
Before receiving assistance under the National Fellowship for Scheduled Caste Students (NFSC) Scheme, Ajay faced financial constraints and difficulties in meeting educational expenses. His family had limited resources to support the costs associated with higher education, making it challenging to manage the financial requirements of doctoral studies while pursuing his academic goals.
The NFSC Scheme has provided Ajay with financial assistance to support his Ph.D. studies. His fellowship assistance commenced in January 2024 and includes fellowship, House Rent Allowance (HRA) and contingency support. The reported amount of assistance availed is Rs 40,700.
The support has helped address financial constraints, educational expenses and limitations in accessing the resources required for research. With this assistance, Ajay has been able to devote greater attention to his research and academic responsibilities, easing some of the financial pressure associated with pursuing doctoral studies.
Since receiving support under the scheme, Ajay reports improvements in his academic performance and his ability to focus on research. The assistance has also strengthened his confidence and improved his outlook towards future career opportunities. It has helped him continue working towards his long-term goal of completing his PhD and building a successful professional career.
Ajay Kumar’s experience highlights the importance of financial assistance in enabling scholars from financially constrained backgrounds to pursue advanced education. By helping reduce economic barriers, the NFSC Scheme supports students in continuing their academic journeys and working towards their aspirations in research and higher education.
His journey reflects how targeted educational support can help scholars remain focused on their studies, strengthen their confidence and move closer to their academic and professional goals.

The PAIMANA-Performance Monitoring Dashboard provides a unified digital interface for monitoring sector-wise performance with interactive visualization and time-series analysis for improved accessibility for policymakers, researchers and stakeholders.

title: Ministry of Textiles Organized Workshops on Cyber Security & Secure Digital Disposal and E-Waste Management Awareness under Special Campaign 6
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 11:42AM by PIB Delhi
content:
As part of Special Campaign 6, the Ministry of Textiles organised workshops on E-Waste Management Awareness and Cyber Security & Secure Digital Disposal on 15 October 2026, with the participation of over 85 officials, including all Nodal Officers. The workshops aimed to promote responsible e-waste management, strengthen cyber security awareness and encourage safe digital practices in the workplace.
A dedicated
Cyber Security Awareness Session was organised
to familiarise officials and staff with emerging cyber threats, including phishing attacks, malware, fraudulent WhatsApp messages and digital arrest scams. The session highlighted the importance of identifying suspicious emails, links, attachments and messages, particularly those impersonating known contacts or seeking money, one-time passwords (OTPs) or personal information.
Participants were advised to exercise caution while handling digital communications, refrain from clicking on unknown links or downloading unverified files, avoid sharing sensitive information, and verify the authenticity of suspicious communications before taking any action. The session also emphasised the importance of cyber hygiene, vigilance and the timely reporting of cyber incidents to safeguard official and personal information.
The
E-Waste Management Awareness session
sensitised officials to the adverse environmental impact of improper e-waste disposal, including soil and water contamination and the release of hazardous substances that may pose risks to human health and ecosystems. They highlighted the importance of resource conservation through the reuse, refurbishment and recycling of electronic equipment, wherever feasible, to recover valuable materials, reduce the demand for raw materials and minimise the volume of waste sent to landfills. Officials were also made aware of the need for proper segregation, safe handling and disposal of obsolete electronic and electrical equipment through authorised channels, in accordance with applicable e-waste management rules.
The sessions encouraged the adoption of sustainable office practices, emphasising that responsible e-waste management contributes to environmental protection, efficient resource utilisation and the promotion of a circular economy.
These initiatives reflect the Ministry of Textiles’ commitment to promoting a cleaner workplace, ensuring responsible resource management and fostering a secure digital environment. By integrating environmental sustainability with cyber security awareness, the Ministry continues to advance the objectives of Special Campaign 6 through improved workplace practices, resource conservation and enhanced digital safety.
The Ministry has also undertaken initiatives for the collection and proper management of e-waste generated within its premises, emphasising the responsible disposal of obsolete and discarded electronic and electrical equipment in accordance with applicable guidelines.
Electronic and electrical equipment that has reached the end of its useful life, including desktop computers, keyboards, photocopiers (Xerox machines), air purifiers and electric hot cases, requires proper handling and disposal in accordance with applicable e-waste management regulations.
The initiative highlights the importance of identifying obsolete electronic and electrical equipment, ensuring its appropriate segregation and facilitating its disposal through authorized channels. Responsible e-waste management helps prevent environmental pollution, supports the recovery of valuable materials and promotes the efficient use of resources.
The Ministry encourages awareness among officials and staff regarding sustainable office practices and the importance of proper e-waste disposal. Such efforts contribute towards a cleaner working environment and the broader national objective of sustainable development.
Through these initiatives, the Ministry of Textiles reiterates its commitment to responsible resource management, environmental sustainability and digital safety. The activities reinforce the objectives of Special Campaign 6 by promoting cleanliness, proper disposal of obsolete equipment, efficient resource utilisation and a secure digital environment across its offices.

title: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports issues operational guidelines for revised Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs)
subtitle:
New strategic components for India’s long-term sporting vision, CWG 2030, and the 2036 Olympic bid

ANSF supports Indian athletes in preparing for major international sporting events
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 4:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports has issued the operational guidelines for the revised Scheme of Assistance to National Sports Federations (NSFs), which include revised norms of assistance for various components of the Scheme, following the Government’s approval for continuation of the Scheme for the period 2026-27 to 2030-31 (16th Finance Commission Cycle) at a total outlay of ₹7,386.74 crore.
The Scheme is the principal mechanism for supporting India’s athletes in preparation for major international events such as the Olympic Games, Asian Games, Commonwealth Games, Paralympic Games and World Championships.
The Scheme provides support for the conduct of National coaching camps, training in academies and athlete support including boarding, lodging, sports kits, insurance and sports science services, engagement of foreign coaches, High Performance Directors and support personnel such as physiotherapists, sports scientists and doctors, Foreign exposure through international training and competitions, conduct of Senior, Junior and Sub-Junior National Championships, Grassroots and junior athlete development and administrative and governance support to NSFs.
In the revised Scheme, several new strategic components have been included, aligning with India’s long-term sporting vision and preparations for the 2036 Olympic bid and Commonwealth Games 2030.
Enhancement in amount of assistance for hosting international sports events
: Under the revised Scheme, there is a substantive enhancement in the financial assistance for hosting international tournaments in India. Now, financial support up to Rs. 50 crore can be provided to NSFs for hosting an international event, depending upon the nature and importance of the event, number of participating countries and athletes. Proposals of NSFs will be assessed by a designated Committee headed by Secretary (Sports).
Training at Olympic Training Centres
: Presently, coaching/training of the athletes preparing for mega-international sporting events, including Olympics, is done at National Centres of Excellence (NCOEs), academies and private sports facilities, as well as in foreign training facilities. To provide specialised training of high standards, Olympic Training Centres (OTCs) equipped with the latest sports science equipment are being planned to be set up, and these centres will be dedicated to one sport, having the best modern training facilities and experts, which will reduce the reliance on overseas training of Indian athletes. The Indian elite athletes training at such OTCs will be supported towards coaches and technical staff, Sports science services, and specialized equipment and technical support.
Support for National Games
: Taking into consideration the importance of the National Games and the need to organize them in a befitting manner and scale, provision has been made in the revised Scheme to provide assistance up to Rs. 50 crore for conduct of National Games towards sports equipment, Timing, Scoring and Result (TSR) services, remuneration to Technical officials and technical conduct.
Assistance to NSFs of indigenous sports for global outreach
: For spreading global outreach of indigenous games, a component of support to NSFs of indigenous games has been included in the revised Scheme for assisting in efforts of NSFs for inclusion as demonstration events in global competitions like the Olympics, Asian Games or Commonwealth Games, in establishment of national federations in other countries across the world, providing requisite support to international federations/continental federations of indigenous sports having their offices in India etc.
International sports cooperation initiatives with Global South countries
: India has High Performance Centres and training facilities, both at SAI Centres and non- SAI Centres, which can position the country as a leading partner for Global South by facilitating training of athletes and coaches by providing scholarships and subsidised use of facilities. Provision of assistance towards international cooperation has been included in the revised Scheme.
Support for sports competitions organized for multi-lateral bodies such as BRICS, BIMSTEC
: Under the revised Scheme, provision of financial assistance for conduct of sports competitions, sport-related conferences, meetings, research works, workshops, organized for multi-lateral bodies such as BRICS, BIMSTEC and any other similar multi-lateral body has been included.
Support to recognized international/ continental bodies having offices in India
: For supporting recognized international/continental bodies in India, the revised Scheme includes a component of funding to NSF/NOC for extending the required support on a case-to-case basis, as per the recommendation of the designated Committee headed by Secretary (Sports).

title: Polish Youth Delegation Completes Second Edition of Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme
ministry: Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 12:24PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The second edition of the Jamsaheb Memorial Youth Exchange Programme was held from 7 to 14 October 2026. A 19-member Polish youth delegation visited Gujarat, Maharashtra and New Delhi. The programme comprised of visits to sites of shared historical significance, cultural engagements, visits to institutions showcasing India’s scientific, economic and cultural development and interactions with senior Indian leadership.
The programme was announced by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi during his State visit to Poland in August 2024 and forms part of the Five-Year Action Plan (2024–2028) for the India–Poland Strategic Partnership. It envisages an annual exchange of Polish youth to India, providing participants with opportunities to explore the country’s history, culture, institutions and contemporary development.
A major highlight of the programme was the visit to the Balachadi Polish Children’s Camp Memorial in Jamnagar, Gujarat, which commemorates the humanitarian contribution of Maharaja Jam Saheb Digvijaysinhji Ranjitsinhji Jadeja. During the Second World War, the Maharaja provided refuge, education and medical care to Polish children displaced by the war. His compassion earned him the enduring recognition of
Dobry Maharaja
, or the Good Maharaja, in Poland. The visit offered the delegation an opportunity to learn about this remarkable chapter of shared history and the enduring bonds between the two countries.
Thereafter, the delegation visited the Valivade Polish Refugee Camp Memorial in Kolhapur, Maharashtra, which commemorates the refuge provided to thousands of Polish refugees during and after the Second World War.
The visits to Balachadi and Valivade highlighted India’s humanitarian support to the Polish people during a difficult period and reinforced the historical foundations of India–Poland friendship.
In New Delhi, the Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports, Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya, hosted the Polish youth delegation for an interaction over dinner. The engagement provided an opportunity for the visiting youth to interact with the Minister, exchange perspectives and learn about India’s approach to youth development and participation. The interaction underscored the importance of people-to-people exchanges in fostering mutual understanding and strengthening ties between India and Poland.
The delegates expressed their gratitude for the opportunity to explore India’s rich history and cultural heritage over the course of seven-days. Visits to the Jamsaheb and Valivade camp memorials, Dandi Kutir in Gandhinagar and Kirti Mandir in Porbandar, the birthplace of Mahatma Gandhi, were among the memorable experiences of the programme. The delegates appreciated the warm hospitality extended to them and described the visit as an enriching experience that had deepened their understanding of India and strengthened their connection with the country.
The delegation also had the opportunity to call on External Affairs Minister Dr. S. Jaishankar and interact with him on matters relating to India–Poland relations and the role of youth exchanges in strengthening bilateral ties.
The successful completion of the second edition reinforces the importance of youth diplomacy in advancing India–Poland relations. By connecting young people with shared history and contemporary India, the programme carries forward the legacy of Maharaja Jam Saheb and strengthens the enduring friendship between the two countries.

title: Navigating India’s Waterways: Building a Safer, Smarter Network
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 12:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
India is building a safer and smarter inland navigation ecosystem as waterway traffic expands. Hydrographic surveys and fairway maintenance keep channels navigable, while India’s first riverine lighthouses on the Brahmaputra add long-range support for 24×7 navigation. Digital platforms provide real-time depth, route and weather information. Together, these interventions are strengthening navigation safety, improving predictability and supporting the growing movement of cargo across India’s waterways.
Strengthening Navigation as Waterways Expand
India’s rivers and waterways are gaining a larger role in the country’s transport network. They are being energised as a force multiplier for the economy, offering a cost-efficient and cleaner mode for transportation. Moving a tonne of freight by water costs roughly one-third of road transport and half of rail. It also generates a fraction of the carbon emissions. This eases pressure on highways and reserves them for passengers and time-sensitive goods.
The country has
111 National Waterways (NW)
to promote shipping and navigation. The total length of these waterways is 20,187 km, spread across 23 States and 4 Union Territories. Of these,
32 National Waterways
are currently operational. The growing economic value of waterways is reflected in their rapidly increasing freight movement. Cargo movement on inland waterways rose from
29 million metric tonnes (MMT)
in 2014–15 to
218 MMT
in 2025–26. This represents a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of
20.13%
. The growth has already surpassed the target of 200 MMT set under
Maritime India Vision 2030
. Inland waterways are therefore moving from potential to performance.
This expansion of waterways is making it necessary to provide for safer and smarter navigation support and infrastructure that help understand river conditions and navigability across routes. Hydrographic surveys and fairway maintenance are being done to help vessels navigate changing river conditions. Digital platforms are providing information on depths, routes, vessel movement and weather. New navigation infrastructure, including India’s first riverine lighthouses, is adding further support for round-the-clock movement.
Hydrographic Surveys:
Knowing the Rivers
A river may appear unchanged from the surface, but the structure of its navigable channel is not visible from outside. Water levels also vary across seasons and river stretches. These changes can affect the route available to vessels. For this reason, inland waterway development requires continuous knowledge of river conditions.
Hydrographic surveys
Hydrography involves measuring and describing water bodies and their physical features, like structure of the bed, water depth, flow direction and possible hazards. The purpose is to support navigation and other activities like offshore operations, scientific research, environmental protection and forecasting services. A key objective of hydrographic surveys is to produce navigation charts and maps that provide a clear, comprehensive and updated picture of the surveyed area.
The
Inland Waterways Authority of India
conducts hydrographic surveys across National Waterways. These surveys measure and analyse river depths, bed profiles, shoals, flow characteristics and morphological changes affecting navigability.
These include
thalweg surveys
that identify and monitor the deepest navigable channel along the river stretch.
Terminal & jetty surveys
assess depth and approach conditions near terminals and jetties, etc.
Continuous hydrographic assessment supports navigational channel (fairway) development, dredging plans, navigational safety and informed decisions for inland water transport (IWT) infrastructure development across the country.
Dredging is the process of removing sediments from the bottom of water bodies. Dredging work is carried out across stretches of National Waterways in order to improve their navigability.
River conditions can change rapidly in some stretches. Survey frequency therefore varies according to the requirements of individual waterways. As of
September 2026
, regular thalweg surveys covered
22 National Waterways
. Surveys are conducted weekly, fortnightly or monthly, depending on the waterway. The Indian portion of Indo-Bangladesh Protocol route was also covered under this monitoring system. This is an inland water transit network that enables cargo movement between India and Bangladesh through designated river routes.
Least Available Depth: A Critical Navigation Parameter
One of the most important outputs of hydrographic surveys is the
Least Available Depth (LAD)
. LAD refers to the minimum depth of water available in a navigation channel. It is assessed for a particular stretch and a specific period. LAD directly influences vessel operations and navigation planning. It determines the permissible vessel draft and influences cargo-carrying capacity. It also supports route scheduling and seasonal navigation decisions.
Aids to Navigation: Guiding Vessels Safely
Safe navigation depends on reliable systems that help vessels identify routes, hazards and changing conditions. Under the Marine Aids to Navigation Act, 2021, these systems are formally recognised as
Aids to Navigation (AtoN)
.
An AtoN is a device, system or service external to vessels that is designed and operated to enhance safe and efficient navigation of individual vessels and vessel traffic. These include lighted buoys, radar beacons, lamp posts, channel markers, lighthouses, lightships, etc.
Buoys
- Floating objects anchored at a definite location to guide or warn mariners, to mark positions of submerged objects, or to moor vessels in lieu of anchoring. Type of buoys include lateral marks, cardinal marks, isolated danger marks, safe water marks, special marks, emergency wreck marking buoy.
Radar beacon (Racon)
- Highly responsive, single piece device used by ports and harbor authorities to help mariners easily identify the location of fixed or floating Aids to Navigation. The device transmits in almost any type of weather, unaffected by fog or poor weather and sea conditions.
The Directorate General of Lighthouses and Lightships (DGLL) is responsible for the development, maintenance and management of general AtoN along India’s coastline. It also serves as the national authority for training on AtoN and Vessel Traffic Services (VTS). India is a signatory to the International Convention for the Safety of Life at Sea (SOLAS), which requires contracting governments to develop and operate appropriate aids to navigation. India also follows the recommendations and guidelines on Aids to Navigation (AtoN) issued by the International Organization for Marine Aids to Navigation (IALA).
Across the national waterways, IWAI maintains a robust system of AToN. Different waterways use different combinations of these aids based on navigation requirements.
National Waterway-3
is a strong example of this infrastructure. NW-3, located in the State of Kerala, forms a critical component of the country’s inland water transport network. The West Coast Canal system, connects Kottapuram to Kollam and extends through the Champakkara and Udyogamandal Canals. The entire navigable stretch is equipped with AtoN to support 24×7 navigation.
A total
of 312 solar-powered lighted FRP
(Fiberglass Reinforced Plastic) buoys and
17 beacon lamp posts
are deployed along this waterway.
Riverine Lighthouses:
Bringing 24×7 Navigation Support
India’s inland navigation system entered new territory in March 2026. India announced its
first four riverine lighthouses
on the Brahmaputra, designated as National Waterway-2. The development marks a significant step in strengthening Aids to Navigation on inland waterways. The four lighthouses are being established at
Pandu, Bogibeel, Silghat and Biswanath Ghat
. The
₹74-crore project
will combine navigational guidance with modern monitoring capabilities.
The lighthouses will rise 20 metres above ground, providing prominent navigational reference points.
Their geographical range will extend to 14 nautical miles, supporting wider navigational visibility.
Their luminous range will extend between 8 and 10 nautical miles, aiding night-time vessel movement.
Powered entirely by solar energy, it will provide a clean and reliable source for lighthouse operations.
Weather-observation sensors will provide additional information relevant to navigation and safety.
The complexes will also feature museums, amphitheatres, cafeterias and landscaped public spaces.
Children’s play areas and souvenir shops will add public and tourism-oriented facilities.
Why This Matters for the Brahmaputra
The initiative marks the first deployment of lighthouse infrastructure on an inland waterway in India. It brings a new navigation-safety mechanism to a river corridor with growing transport activity. NW-2 connects Assam's
Dhubri to Sadiya
across a navigable length of
891 kilometres
. It is the longest navigable stretch of any Indian waterway.
The waterway supports movement of cargo, passengers and tourists across the region. It also serves supply chains associated with
tea, coal and fertiliser
. Cargo movement on NW-2 increased from
0.90 million metric tonnes (MMT) in FY 2024–25 to 1.29 MMT in FY 2025–26
. This reinforces the need for stronger navigational infrastructure along the waterway. The new lighthouses will support
24×7 navigation
. The project therefore combines navigation safety, technological support and tourism development along the Brahmaputra.
Digital Navigation & Real-Time Information
Technology is transforming how vessels navigate India’s inland waterways. Digital platforms bring together information on waterways, vessel movement, depth, weather and traffic. This enables mariners and authorities to access critical information when and where it is needed.
Digital Hydrographic Charts: Putting River Information on Screen
Navigation information is provided digitally to Mariners for enhanced safety through modern hydrographic charts. As of September 2026,
Electronic Navigational Charts (ENCs)
have been prepared for
18 operational and tidal waterways
. They are uploaded on portals like
PANI
and
IWAI Vessel Tracker
. Before 2014, this facility was available only on
NW-1
(the Ganga - Bhagirathi - Hooghly river system between Haldia and Prayagraj). Its expansion represents a significant widening of digitally accessible navigation information. The charts complement physical surveys by translating river information into a navigation-ready format.
PANI and IWAI Vessel Tracker: Connecting Navigation with Real-Time Information
Navigation involves more than knowing channel depth. The Portal for Asset and Navigation Information (PANI) brings river navigation and infrastructure information on a single platform. PANI provides details about National Waterways and associated assets. These include fairways, infrastructure facilities and cross-river structures. The portal also provides jetty connectivity and emergency services for facilitating transportation of cargo.
The IWAI Vessel Tracker and PANI Portal together form a web and mobile-based e-navigation system. It provides real-time vessel tracking, updated navigation routes and depth information. These features support safe and efficient movement on inland waterways.
Naudarshika: Towards Integrated River Traffic Management
Naudarshika, the National River Traffic and Navigation System, has been launched in 2025 for safe, efficient and sustainable vessel movement. The system incorporates real-time Least Available Depth (LAD) information to support navigation. Alongside existing digital platforms such as PANI and LADIS, Naudarshika adds a dedicated system for river traffic and navigation management.
River Information Services: A Traffic Information Network
River Information Services take digital navigation a step further. RIS combines vessel tracking technologies, weather and water sensors and information technology systems. It provides real-time data to vessel operators and authorities. It also supports communication between vessels and control centres. This exchange supports better traffic management and faster operational decisions.
RIS on the Ganga
RIS has been implemented on National Waterway-1 (Ganga) across three stretches. These are Haldia–Farakka, Farakka–Patna and Patna–Varanasi. The system includes
4 control stations
and
13 base stations
. It incorporates Automatic Identification System (AIS)equipment and Very High Frequency (VHF) communication. Meteorological sensors are also part of the network. RIS consoles have been provided on 30 departmental vessels. Together, these components create a real-time traffic-monitoring system along NW-1.
A Connected Approach to Safer Navigation
Safe navigation on India’s waterways is built on continuous knowledge, reliable infrastructure and timely information. Hydrographic surveys help understand changing river conditions, while navigation aids provide visible guidance on the water. Digital platforms are adding another layer of precision through real-time depth, route, weather and traffic information. Together, these systems are making inland navigation more predictable and responsive. As waterway traffic expands, this integrated approach helps create a stronger foundation for safe, efficient and round-the-clock vessel movement.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported assault and inhuman treatment of a woman by her husband and family members enraged by her living with another man in Surendranagar district, Gujarat
subtitle:
Notices issued to the District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police, Sundranagar, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

The report to include the status of the victim's health and compensation, if any, paid to her
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 5:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that a married woman, who had been living with another man, was subjected to cruel and inhuman treatment by her husband and family in Surendranagar district, Gujarat. Reportedly, the woman and the man were tracked and brought back under the guise of conducting a 'purification ritual'. The woman was beaten with sticks, kicked and tied to a tree. The accused also allegedly forced the man accompanying her to rape her.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Accordingly, it has issued notices to the District Magistrate and the Superintendent of Police, Surendranagar, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the status of the victim's health and compensation, if any, paid to her.
According to the media report, carried on 8th October 2026, the incident came to light when the video of the incident was circulated on social media.

The report to include the health status of the injured students
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 5:49PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that three students, aged 7 to 8 years, were injured when a portion of the ceiling plaster of their classroom collapsed on them in a dilapidated government primary school building in Udaipur district, Rajasthan. Reportedly, the victims sustained head injuries and teachers were not present in the school when the incident occurred. The injured students walked home on their own and their family members subsequently took them to the hospital for treatment.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Udaipur District Magistrate, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It is expected to include the health status of the injured students.
According to the media report carried on 7th October 2026, the school was ordered to close after the incident and alternate arrangements are being made by the authorities for conducting classes. Reportedly, the school building was last repaired in 2020.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported borewell water contamination due to seepage of chemical-laden factory effluents near Ambad Industrial Area in Nashik district, Maharashtra
subtitle:
Issues a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks

Comments from the Maharashtra State Pollution Control Board also sought
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                16 OCT 2026 5:47PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report that the borewell water in the Dattanagar locality near Ambad Industrial Area in Nashik district, Maharashtra became contaminated due to seepage of chemical-laden effluents, allegedly discharged from factories in the adjoining industrial area. Reportedly, the residents have been receiving contaminated water for the past two months.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of violation of human rights. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Maharashtra Chief Secretary, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks. It has also sought comments from the Maharashtra State Pollution Control Board.
According to the media report, carried on 7th October 2026, children were advised not to attend schools while doctors advised women from the area to avoid pregnancy. The residents spend approximately Rs. 5,000 per month on purchasing clean drinking water, besides incurring a huge amount on medical treatment.
